newsitem.title: UKRAINE: Ukraine's defence ministry sets up cargo carrier.
newsitem.headline: Ukraine's defence ministry sets up cargo carrier.

text.p: Ukraine's defence ministry has set up a new air cargo company and plans to limit the number of private carriers leasing planes from the military from 20 to between six and eight, a ministry spokesman said on Monday.
The ministry's new "Ukrayinska Aviatsiyno-Transportna Kompaniya" (UATC) would use Ilyushin-76 cargo planes, he said.

Last month the defence ministry ordered back all Il-76s leased to cargo firms for check-ups and re-signing of contracts, provoking outrage among private carriers who said they were forced to cancel profitable contracts.
"We have been working with companies on the agreements, which are due to be signed in the near future," he said.
The UATC and private companies would not have more than 40 planes altogether while the rest would continue to be used for military purposes, he added.
The Il-76, made in the Central Asian state of Uzbekistan, can carry 40 tonnes of cargo for 3,500 km (2,200 miles) without refuelling.
Ukraine was home to 182 Il-76s when the former Soviet Union fell apart in 1991. At least 60 of them were leased to private companies.
